answer.rationale:
The memory that would most easily drive a full switch is memory_c2 (low-cost vendor cut unit cost, onboarded fast, clean invoicing). That is exactly why it needs the archive pull: as summarized it records price and invoicing outcomes but says nothing about on-time delivery performance, qualification volume, or whether that vendor ever carried primary volume at the rate we now run. If the original record covers only a partial or low-volume award, it cannot license a full primary migration. memory_c3 is the other load-bearing record — I want to know what share of volume the second source actually absorbed during the shortage and how long qualification took, since that sets whether a 14-day window is realistic.

Current intent: bring the low-cost vendor in as a qualified second source at a deliberately small, guarded allocation rather than switching primary supply. Reasoning: the line is at 94% of committed volume with no buffer, so any qualification stumble converts a cost decision into a missed-delivery event, and the stated objective explicitly forbids increasing delivery risk. A full switch bets the whole volume on one archived cost result; a guarded dual-source award captures part of the mandate now and buys evidence for a larger move at the next review. memory_c4 and memory_c6 (renegotiation, multi-year volume pricing) are noted but currently blocked — the incumbent has refused to reopen price this cycle — so negotiate_terms is not live, and defer_decision is unsafe because the contract does not auto-renew.

Open risks I am not resolving with this decision: a guarded award alone likely does not deliver the full 18% cut this year, so the mandate stays partly unmet and should be escalated rather than quietly absorbed; the 14-day expiry means continuity of the incumbent's volume must be bridged on short terms as part of this award; and the low-cost vendor's quote may not hold once qualification and expediting costs enter total cost of ownership. If the archive shows memory_c2 was itself a full primary migration at comparable volume with delivery data intact, I would revisit scaling up to a staged primary switch — but I will not assume that in advance of the record.
